ordered_diagnoses: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas

s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva
Family history of similar facial papules
Histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells with small cystic spaces
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Approximately 60 lesions are present
Lesions are asymptomatic
Medical history includes a meningioma
Family history of similar facial papules in a daughter
No palmar or plantar pits observed
Histopathology of lesions shows basaloid cells with small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and surrounding stroma is evident
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene

shortlist: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas

shortlist.label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple basaloid skin lesions, a history of meningioma, and a family history of similar lesions, which are all characteristic of this syndrome

shortlist.label: Generalized basaloid follicular hamartoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's skin lesions show basaloid cells with small cystic spaces, consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The histopathology of the lesions shows buds and cords of basaloid cells, which is consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Gorlin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's medical history of meningioma and the presence of multiple skin-colored papules are consistent with this syndrome

shortlist.label: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's family history of similar lesions and the presence of multiple infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas are consistent with this condition

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules, family history of similar lesions, and histopathology showing basaloid cells with small cystic spaces, along with a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, are all consistent with Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome, also known as Gorlin syndrome. The presence of a meningioma also supports this diagnosis, as it is a known association with this syndrome.

rejected.label: Generalized basaloid follicular hamartoma syndrome
rejected.why: While this condition also presents with basaloid follicular hamartomas, the presence of a SUFU gene mutation and the patient's family history of similar lesions are more consistent with Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome

rejected.label: Infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a type of basal cell carcinoma, but the patient's presentation of multiple lesions and family history suggest a genetic syndrome rather than a single type of carcinoma

rejected.label: Gorlin syndrome
rejected.why: Gorlin syndrome is another name for Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome, so it is not a distinct alternative

rejected.label: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas
rejected.why: While this condition involves multiple basal cell carcinomas, the patient's presentation and genetic findings are more consistent with Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
